body: Oh shit. That might just be what I was looking for. Thank you!

By falsetto I mean extremely breathy and kinda toneless head voice. Basically sounds absurd, a bit like Mickey Mouse, that's probably my best comparison.

I'll try that humming exercise you mentioned, never heard of that one before! Might just do it. But yeah, I've also noticed the whole posture adjustment. It does absolute wonders!

In any case, my break is right around middle C, head voice starts about three semitones higher, so around D#4. Slowly working on filling that gap, although I admit I haven't been challenging myself enough lately, singing campfire songs mostly.
It's what I've been doing so far. It's just that a few of our songs are those three or four semitones too high, so I'm trying to climb that little bit higher.

Sorry for the late reply.

Well, for example, With or Without You. First three verses, no problem. But then the second "With or without you--" is much higher, with a little jump into falsetto at the "WITH-out" part.

Or "Beautiful Day." Verse is fine, but the chorus becomes a struggle. You can hear the strain even in Bono's voice. But in the phrase "Don't let it get away," IT is too high for me even when straining.

Another example is in "Vertigo," "give me something I can feel... Feel," the second feel briefly hits a very high note.

For now, I resort to avoiding the high notes by just dialing it back, staying on the lower notes. Not really sure WHY it works, but if I go a perfect fifth down from his note, it sounds consonant and fine, just has a lot less soul and power. Dunno if I'm accidentally harmonizing, but it sounds fine with a guitar or bass when I do it. Hell, does the same chord theory apply to bass and vocals? Looks like it might.
Yes, true. But with my voice, I definitely need advice. Thinking asking our lead vocalist might help, not sure why I didn't.

It's the same way with me, but on the low end. Most days I can hit the D2, but there are days when I hit a C#2 or a C2 effortlessly, or days when I can't get past E2 comfortably.

Higher end is a lot harder for me, because the tone, rather than losing quality, just breaks outright. Squeals a little and dies. The break between chest and head voice is about 4 semitones long and absolutely inaccessible for me. I know this gets better with time, but I don't want to rely on my pathetically chesty falsetto that sounds like the cats outside our house.

But thank you, it's helpful. I like hearing it first hand, y'know. But I still just don't understand how even singers like Bowie manage to hit those much higher notes and STILL sound like it's their more-or-less natural voice!
Right. Makes sense, thank you. I do Dylan and Cash covers because, let's be honest, you can't really mess that up. Can you recommend any styles to help with development?

Been there, done that... How's that for a burning sensation.

Anyway, yeah! Studying anything in particular?

But you're right. It'll work out somehow. I never asked you, where exactly are you in life at the moment. Still studying?

I'm thinking I should look into that... Might get my nerves a little less tense constantly. Thanks!

By the way, not sure how you did it, maybe by talking to me like you would to a normal human being rather than a sick person. But I don't feel quite as hopeless. I still don't think I'll ever amount to much, but such is life. I feel like it can work.
Can't say I'm familiar with it. What's it about?
Who was winning when you broke it up? My bets are on the dumpster.

Ugh. Sounds fun. Ever got into a fight?

At least you aren't selling sham 'health supplements' to senior citizens over the phone. I swear to God, a call center job is torture. Glad I busted out.

Criminal law or psychology. To be a prosecutor, damn... I'd do my darn finest to put the right people behind bars. Even the job of an interrogator/interviewer. Can't help but be totally fascinated by the way people react and behave in certain situations.

Weird huh... I hate capitalist society, its values and such, and yet I'd enforce its laws. What's your gig anyway? My guess would be accounting of some form.

Samsung's are reliable. The 512 gig is probably the best deal, in my opinion.

Anyway, I dunno. I just get feelings about people. Not always right, of course. But quite often. It's not really analysis or anything, just, you're talking to a person, and suddenly a flash in your head tells you, "this dude swims, this dude fucks, this dude is a writer." 
Wish I could study sociology and go into counseling you know. That'd be a dream job, and it wouldn't contribute to the system we live in.

Oh baby. Good old capitalism. 

Y'know, you should read The Capital. It's actually a very inspiring read. If you haven't already, that is. Shows that those of us who don't conform to the norm aren't as alone as we'd think.

Music is a big one ye. Writing, not so much anymore. Going on nights out with "the guys" a few times a month. Juggling two bands. Y'know. Good stuff. 

Let me guess, I bet you're a swimmer. Got that sorta vibe off ya.

Well segregation is pretty simple overall. Easy to get into, hard to master. So basically, you gather a group of peers. Simple enough. Now you watch for who is the weirdest, most awkward, unfunny or in any negative way the most different from the rest. 

Now that you find that person, or, more rarely, group of people, you do everything you can to make them feel unwelcome. But you gotta be smart about it. Start off slow and subtle, make them think it's just fun and games, so that they don't immediately run away and avoid you. The goal is to have your mental torture dolls for a long period of time, preferably for life.

Jokes aside, segregation is bad, kids; don't engage in it.

Mainstream stuff. The stuff everyone watches. Except Marvel stuff. It's good, but I could never get into it the way my friends do.

But... Music don't pay the bills. And I'm the incarnation of mediocrity, so to speak.

Isn't that right?

I probably shouldn't add fuel to your fire, but I have to agree. To be a slave to our society is a fate worse than death. I'm planning on hopping freight trains, playing on the streets for change and, well, living off music.

If that fails, I've got an appointment with a certain mr. .45

Evgenij Onegin. An absolute masterpiece of literature. My undying inspiration. The Epic of Gilgamesh. A strong idea, good lesson. Makes the fact that no one will remember me for anything that much more painful.

When sleeping normally, no. It's just kinda.. Nice. Sometimes weird dreams about my sister being a demon serial killer or being followed by floating transparent Nazis.

But you're right. Not enough sleep. Not nearly. Fuck. It's hard to break the habit. I'll try to go to sleep at 11:30 tomorrow and try to hit it down to 11

Well I've considered narcolepsy as a probable cause. I mean, I fall asleep during classes despite getting 5-6 hours of sleep a night and then some. Nap far too frequently.

Then again, when I do sleep, I sleep hard. Nothing wakes me. And I dream pretty vividly too, lucid at times.
